editorialDecl.p: Text transcribed by OCR (Humanitext OCR v2, Gemini models) from the scans named in the source description. Structure (div, quote, head): assigned automatically from printed cues (Bekker references before lemmata, section numbers, headings, book titles, lecture headings; in the paraphrases, Aristotle's chapters located from the running heads) and reviewed by the editors at every boundary that was not certain. In works divided into lectures (Πρᾶξις, Θεωρία) the lectures are divs; topic headings that run across lectures (e.g. Περὶ οὐσίας) are marked milestone[@unit='topic'] and kept as text. Text: OCR of the page images (gemini-3-flash-preview; gemini-3.7-flash where it failed), collated word by word, page by page and in five-line blocks, with the First1KGreek transcription of the same edition (tlg4034.tlg005.1st1K-grc1). Lines on which the two disagreed, lines without a First1KGreek counterpart and lines containing a word form not attested in a Greek form lexicon (about two fifths of the lines) were read again from images of the single lines by a second model (gemini-3.8-flash); words still undecided were read line by line by a third model (gemini-3.1-pro-preview). A reading was adopted when the re-reading of the image agreed with it; the remaining words were decided on the page image by student assistants or by AI-assisted checking under the editor's supervision. Lines on which the OCR agreed word for word with First1KGreek and whose words are all attested were not re-read. No text was copied from First1KGreek (Open Greek and Latin Project, University of Leipzig; CC BY-SA 4.0): it served only as a collation witness, and every disagreement was decided from the page image of this edition. Spelling, accents and breathings follow the printed page: the models were instructed to transcribe exactly as printed and the checkers chose the printed form, but a normalised accentuation adopted by a model may occasionally remain. Later checks against the page images (line numbers, marginal references, signs and apparatus, omitted lines) are listed in the revision description. Headings inside a div (sub-headings, closing formulas, labels of tables) are ab[@type='head']. The words of diagrams and tables are not body text: each diagram or table is given once as figure after the last body line printed before it (labels, trees and tables transcribed; pure geometry described in figDesc); where the edition counts the rows of a diagram or table as lines, those line numbers are not used by any lb. Evident misprints of the printed edition, identified on the page image, are kept and given with the correct form as choice/sic/corr; mere variants of spelling or accentuation are left as printed. Misprinted numbers in milestones (Bekker references, old-edition page, folio, column and line numbers), which cannot carry choice/sic/corr, are given with the corrected value where the sequence of the numbers determines it. Where it does not, the printed number is kept (the Aldine line number 5 at p. 146.31). Line breaks: one lb per printed line; @n is the line count of the CAG page (headings included), resynchronised on the printed marginal numbers of the left margin; lines the edition does not count carry lb without @n. Words hyphenated across lines are joined and the lb is placed at the following word boundary. pb/@facs points to the image of the page in the Internet Archive item named in the source description (BookReader page image; for pages supplied from another copy, that copy). Critical-apparatus entries are attached to the line(s) they cite as note[@type='apparatus'] with @target on the lb (line level; the lemma words of an entry are not linked); entries that cannot be resolved remain as note[@type='footnote'] at the page end. References in the margins to older editions or manuscripts are milestone[@type='alt-edition'] with @unit and @ed (the edition identified from the preface of the volume); CAG's repetition of the current old-edition page or folio beside the first line of each page is not encoded. Bekker references printed before lemmata are milestone[@unit='bekker']. Marginal digits fused into the text by OCR have been removed.
